Report DescriptionON 16 APRIL 2021, WE IDENTIFIED A POSSIBLE DEVIATION IN THE TYPICAL CONSUMPTION OF THRUSTER PROPELLER SHAFT SEAL OIL ON ONE OF THE THRUSTERS ON THE MOBILE OFFSHORE DRILLING UNIT, NOBLE GLOBETROTTER II (9600786) WITH NO CORRESPONDING SHEEN OBSERVED. THE MECHANICAL SEAL SYSTEM DESIGNED BY THE OEM IS NOT CONDUCIVE TO COLLECTING DETAILED MEASUREMENTS OF FLUID LEVEL CHANGES AT SUCH A MINOR LEVEL. IN AN EFFORT TO DETERMINE WHETHER THE SEALS WERE FUNCTIONING AS DESIGNED OR IF THERE HAD BEEN A POTENTIAL REPORTABLE DISCHARGE OF SEAL OIL TO THE ENVIRONMENT, WE INITIATED AN INVESTIGATION AND DIALOG WITH THE THRUSTER AND SEAL OEMS AS TO PERFORMANCE AND MONITORING OF THE SEAL OIL FOR THE MECHANICAL PROPELLER SHAFT SEAL OF OUR THRUSTERS. IN THE MIDST OF THIS INVESTIGATION, THE VESSEL WAS IMPACTED BY HURRICANE IDA AND SUSTAINED SOME DAMAGE. THE NOBLE GLOBETROTTER II HAS SINCE GONE IN TO PORT IN FOR SHIPYARD WORK (PASCAGOULA, MS), DURING WHICH TIME WE INTEND TO CHANGE OUT CERTAIN THRUSTERS AND TO COMPLETE OUR INVESTIGATION OF THIS ISSUE IN COORDINATION WITH THE THRUSTER OEM AND THE SHAFT SEAL OEM. WE WILL UPDATE THIS REPORT IF WE CONCLUDE THAT THERE HAS BEEN A REPORTABLE DISCHARGE.

THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 6.8 NMI IN LENGTH AND UP TO 1.2 NMI IN WIDTH, WIDENING APPRECIABLY WITH DISTANCE FROM THE SUSPECTED SOURCE, PARTICULARLY IN THE SOUTHERN HALF OF THE ANOMALY. WINDS AROUND THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE FROM THE SOUTHEAST AT AROUND 8 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: NO KNOWN OIL SPILLS WERE REPORTED NEAR THIS LOCATION. Report Description
**UPDATE TO A PREVIOUS NRC REPORT** THE RP IS REPORTING A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS DUE TO A THIRD PARTY STRIKING AN UNDERGROUND PIPELINE. THE INCIDENT INVOLVES A FARMING TILING MACHINE. RP REPORTS THERE WAS AN IGNITION DUE TO THE STRIKE AND THE LOCAL FD REPORTS THAT THERE WERE TWO (2) INJURIES AND TWO (2) REPORTED FATALITIES. RP STATED THE TWO INJURED INDIVIDUALS WERE TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL. RP STATED THAT THE LOCAL FIRE CHIEF CONFIRMED THE TWO FATALITIES. NO REPORTED EVACUATIONS. THE AREA WAS SECURED AND ROADS WERE CLOSED. THE AMOUNT RELEASED IS BELIEVED TO EXCEED THE 3000 MCF. DAMAGE COST ARE CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. **THE LINE IS CLASS 1, DOT REGULATED. 20" DIAMETER, .281 WALL THICKNESS. X40 GRADE. **MAOP IS 800. OPERATING PRESSURE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS IN THE LOW 700S. 13.6 MILES OF PIPE WAS ISOLATED IN RESPONSE TO THE INCIDENT. **ORIGINAL NRC# 1198853** CALLER REPORTS A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF NATURAL GAS INTO AIR CAUSED BY AN UNKNOWN REASON FROM A PIPELINE.

THE SLICK APPEARED DARK IN COLOR AND HAD SILVER/WHITE SHIMMER TO PART OF THE SLICK. IT HAD SHARP UNNATURAL TURNS BUT FALSE POSITIVES WITH SIMILAR CONTRAST WERE SEEN NEARBY. CONFIDENCE WAS DETERMINED TO BE MEDIUM-HIGH SINCE A POINT SOURCE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED AND THERE WERE FALSE POSITIVES WITH SIMILAR CONTRAST NEARBY. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE WERE MULTIPLE OIL FACILITIES IN THE AREA BUT A DIRECT POINT SOURCE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED.
